propositions: Context-limit escalation silently relocates calls from configured provider-qualified models to bare Anthropic model ids when the model-class table is unconfigured, causing hard failures or unbudgeted spend in provider-isolated environments

Pass-1 entry rung resolution through model-class vocabulary is bypassed during escalation; _rung_target derives escalation targets from module constants and ladder without consulting the run's actual model
Bedrock-qualified primary model and bare Anthropic escalation target create invalid composite ids like 'bedrock:claude-opus-4-8' that fail in Bedrock environments
The one-criterion retry substitutes bare Anthropic ids for provider-qualified primaries on every common case, not just deep-escalation scenarios

Fix threads the run's primary model into _rung_target and applies provider-agreement rule: return primary verbatim if providers match or are undeterminable; drop rungs whose targets have incompatible providers on higher rungs
Unnameable higher rungs are dropped safely rather than crossed, preserving escalation's too-big failure finding while preventing silent provider jumps
